summary.headline: The homepage and other primary marketing pages reduce to 8 characters of visible text ('Duolingo') for a non-JavaScript-executing fetcher; the site's own no-JS fallback -- a real, substantive 1,307-character page -- exists but is unreachable by exactly this kind of fetcher because it is wired through a <noscript><meta http-equiv="refresh"> redirect, a mechanism only a JS-disabled *browser* interprets, not a plain HTTP client — critical severity, Serve the existing /nojs/splash content (or equivalent server-rendered text) directly at the primary marketing URLs for requests that do not execute JavaScript, rather than relying on a <noscript> meta-refresh that only legacy JS-disabled browsers will follow.

findings.title: The homepage and other primary marketing pages reduce to 8 characters of visible text ('Duolingo') for a non-JavaScript-executing fetcher; the site's own no-JS fallback -- a real, substantive 1,307-character page -- exists but is unreachable by exactly this kind of fetcher because it is wired through a <noscript><meta http-equiv="refresh"> redirect, a mechanism only a JS-disabled *browser* interprets, not a plain HTTP client
findings.evidence: A plain fetch to https://www.duolingo.com/, /courses and /blog each return HTTP 200 but reduce to 8 characters of visible text ('Duolingo', the title) after stripping markup and scripts; /press yields only 73. Zero JSON-LD exists on any of these. However, the homepage does contain a <noscript> block: '<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=/nojs/splash">' -- evidence the site deliberately built a fallback for clients that do not execute JavaScript. Fetching that fallback URL directly (https://www.duolingo.com/nojs/splash) confirms it holds real, substantive content: 1,307 characters of genuine marketing copy describing what Duolingo is and how it works. The fallback mechanism does not help a plain HTTP fetcher, though: a <meta http-equiv="refresh"> tag is a browser-interpreted redirect instruction, not something a non-rendering HTTP client (which is how the overwhelming majority of AI retrieval agents actually operate) will ever act on -- it is inert text to them, exactly as it is to this audit's own plain-fetch method. The fallback was built for the JS-disabled-browser case, a shrinking and different population from the non-executing-fetcher case this audit's checks target.

reproduction.observed: 8 on the homepage (and similarly thin on /courses and /blog), versus 1307 on the /nojs/splash fallback page a plain fetcher never reaches
reproduction.expected: The real content already written and hosted at /nojs/splash served directly at the primary URLs for non-JS-executing requests, or exposed via a mechanism a plain HTTP client actually processes (server-side rendering, or at minimum an HTML <a> link rather than a meta-refresh)

suggested_action.summary: Serve the existing /nojs/splash content (or equivalent server-rendered text) directly at the primary marketing URLs for requests that do not execute JavaScript, rather than relying on a <noscript> meta-refresh that only legacy JS-disabled browsers will follow.
suggested_action.mechanism: The content already exists and is already written -- this is a wiring problem, not a content gap. A meta-refresh inside <noscript> assumes the client is a browser rendering the page and choosing not to run JavaScript; an AI agent fetching the page over plain HTTP never gets that far, so the safety net silently does not catch the exact case it appears designed for.
steps: Server-render (or prerender) the homepage and primary marketing pages so real text is present in the initial HTML response.
If a fallback page must remain separate, replace the noscript meta-refresh with content directly inlined in the main response, since a meta-refresh cannot be relied upon to reach non-browser clients.
Add JSON-LD (Organization at minimum) once real server-rendered text exists.
suggested_action.verification: A plain, non-JavaScript-executing fetch to the homepage returns substantive visible text describing Duolingo, matching what /nojs/splash already contains.

not_assessed.check: Structured data, answerability, freshness/corroboration, and engagement (structured-data-audit, answerability-audit, freshness-corroboration-audit, engagement-audit)
not_assessed.reason: The homepage and other primary marketing pages deliver almost no text to a non-JavaScript-executing fetcher (see the render-extractability finding), leaving no prose to derive questions from and no markup-bearing content to check on the pages a plain fetch actually receives. The /nojs/splash fallback page does have real content, but it is not the page these checks would run against in a normal crawl.
not_assessed.impact: Cannot assess whether Duolingo's marketing copy is quotable, current, or well-corroborated, or how an AI-referred visitor experiences a deep page -- genuine gaps in this run, not claims about the site's real, browser-rendered experience, which was not inspected.

not_assessed.reason: No headless-browser engine (Playwright/Puppeteer) was available in this run's environment.
not_assessed.impact: Cannot assess the actual on-site experience for a client that does execute JavaScript.
